title: Practice Exam 2
description: 10 free-response coding challenges covering File I/O, static fields, encapsulation & bounds, interfaces & polymorphism, overloading & constructor chaining, composition, exception-handling input loops, file processing, inheritance & super, and instanceof downcasting.

questions.title: Audit Log
questions.prompt:
Write a program in `Main.java` that creates a file named `audit.log` containing exactly these three lines:

```
[START] System initialized.
[AUTH] User admin verified.
[END] Session terminated.
```

Each line must end with a newline character (`\n`), including the last. If `audit.log` exists, replace its contents cleanly. The program prints nothing to the console.

Use try-with-resources so the file handle is closed and flushed.

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: File audit.log exists with exact text and terminal newline.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Clean Truncation)
tests.description: Truncates existing file containing 50KB of data to exact 3 lines.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Silent Console)
tests.description: No output on System.out or System.err.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Case and Space Precision)
tests.description: Exact bracket formatting [AUTH] and spacing verified.

graderCases.name: Sample run (exact three lines + terminal newline)
Clean truncation of large existing file
Exact bracket/space precision

questions.title: Digital Book
questions.prompt:
Implement the class `DigitalBook` in `DigitalBook.java`; fields must be private.

* A digital book knows its title (`String`) and file size in megabytes (`double`).
* `DigitalBook(String title, double sizeMB)` stores both fields and increments a static download counter.
* `getTitle()` and `getSizeMB()` return the fields; `setSizeMB(double sizeMB)` updates the file size.
* `static int getTotalDownloads()` returns the total number of `DigitalBook` instances created.
* `Main.java` is a test driver; do not edit it.

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: 2 instances created, getters, setter, static downloads returns 2.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Static Isolation)
tests.description: Calling getTotalDownloads() prior to any instantiation returns 0.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Zero File Size)
tests.description: Size 0.0 stores accurately without resetting counter.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Field Encapsulation)
tests.description: All fields confirmed private.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Null Title)
tests.description: new DigitalBook(null, 5.0) increments downloads without crashing.

graderCases.name: Sample run (getters, setter, count)
Zero file size stores, counter increments
Fields private
graderCases.body:
java.lang.reflect.Field t = DigitalBook.class.getDeclaredField("title");
check(java.lang.reflect.Modifier.isPrivate(t.getModifiers()), "title must be private");

graderCases.name: Null title increments cleanly

questions.title: Audio Equalizer
questions.prompt:
Write the class `AudioEqualizer` in `AudioEqualizer.java`; all fields must be private.

* A bass gain level is an integer from -12 to 12 decibels (dB) inclusive.
* `setBass(int bass)` updates the bass level only if it is within `[-12, 12]`; an out-of-range value changes nothing.
* The constructor `AudioEqualizer(int bass)` sends its argument through `setBass`. An invalid initial value leaves the bass at `0`.
* `getBass()` returns the current bass level.
* `boost()` raises the bass by 1 unless it is already 12.
* `cut()` lowers the bass by 1 unless it is already -12.
* `Main.java` is a test driver; do not edit it.

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: Boost to upper limit 12, rejected out-of-range 25, invalid constructor defaults to 0.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Negative Symmetrical Clamp)
tests.description: At -12, calling cut() 5 times remains at -12.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Off-by-One Constructor Rejection)
tests.description: new AudioEqualizer(-13) and new AudioEqualizer(13) default to 0.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Off-by-One Setter Rejection)
tests.description: At 5, calling setBass(13) or setBass(-13) keeps 5.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Exact Minimum Valid Value)
tests.description: new AudioEqualizer(-12) initializes to -12.

graderCases.name: Sample run (boost cap, reject 25, default -20->0)
Negative symmetrical clamp
Off-by-one constructor rejection
graderCases.body:
eq(new AudioEqualizer(-13).getBass(), 0);
eq(new AudioEqualizer(13).getBass(), 0);

graderCases.name: Off-by-one setter rejection
Exact min valid value
graderCases.body:
eq(new AudioEqualizer(-12).getBass(), -12);
eq(new AudioEqualizer(12).getBass(), 12);

questions.title: Medical Clinic Triage
questions.prompt:
Files given (read-only, provided as extra tabs): `Triageable.java` (interface with `String patientName()` and `int urgencyScore()`; the score can be negative), `WalkInPatient.java` and `EmergencyPatient.java` (implement `Triageable`), and `Main.java` (driver). Do not edit them.

Write `ClinicTriage.java` containing two static methods:
* `static int totalUrgency(Triageable[] queue)`: returns the sum of every `urgencyScore()`.
* `static String mostUrgent(Triageable[] queue)`: returns the `patientName()` of the element with the largest `urgencyScore()`.
  * **Tie-Breaking Rule:** On a tie, the first one encountered wins.
  * **Empty Array Rule:** An empty array returns `0` and `""`.
  * **Null Safety:** Skip any `null` elements in `queue` safely.

questions.title: Flight Reservation Overloading
questions.prompt:
Create `FlightBooking` in `FlightBooking.java` with private fields: `String flightCode`, `int seatNumber`, and `boolean firstClass`.

Implement constructor and method overloading:
* `FlightBooking(String flightCode, int seatNumber, boolean firstClass)`: sets all fields.
* `FlightBooking(String flightCode, int seatNumber)`: overloads constructor, defaulting `firstClass` to `false` (chain using `this(...)`).
* `FlightBooking(String flightCode)`: overloads constructor, defaulting `seatNumber` to `30` and `firstClass` to `false` (chain using `this(...)`).
* `getFlightCode()`, `getSeatNumber()`, and `isFirstClass()` return the fields.
* `baggageFee(int bags)`: first bag is free (if bags >= 1); each additional bag costs `$35.00`. If `firstClass` is true, all bags are free (`0.0`).
* `baggageFee(int bags, double overweightFeePerBag)`: overloads `baggageFee` by adding `overweightFeePerBag` to every bag charged (firstClass still receives all bags free).
  * If `bags <= 0`, return `0.0`.

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: 3-arg, 1-arg defaults, baggage fee, overweight fee overload, first class waiver.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Single Bag Boundary)
tests.description: Exactly 1 bag returns 0.0 (first bag is free).

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Zero or Negative Bags)
tests.description: 0 bags or negative bags returns 0.0.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (First Class Overweight Immunity)
tests.description: First class with 10 bags and $100 overweight fee per bag still returns 0.0.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Constructor Chaining Check)
tests.description: Verifies constructor delegation via this(...).

graderCases.name: Sample run (overloads + first class waiver)
Single bag is free
graderCases.body:
FlightBooking b = new FlightBooking("X", 1, false);
eqD(b.baggageFee(1), 0.0);

graderCases.name: Zero or negative bags
First class overweight immunity
graderCases.body:
FlightBooking b = new FlightBooking("X", 1, true);
eqD(b.baggageFee(10, 100.0), 0.0);

questions.title: Car Rental Agreement
questions.prompt:
`Driver.java` is given: `Driver(String name, boolean insuranceVerified)` with `getName()`, `hasInsurance()`, and `setInsurance(boolean insuranceVerified)`. It is provided as an extra tab — do not edit it.

Implement `RentalAgreement.java`; all fields must be private:
* `RentalAgreement(Driver driver, int days, double dailyRate)` stores all three fields.
* `getDriver()` and `getDays()` return the fields; `setDays(int days)` changes the days.
* `cost()`: `days * dailyRate`. If `driver.hasInsurance()` is false, add an uninsured motorist fee of `$15.00` per day (`days * 15.0`).
  * Evaluates `driver.hasInsurance()` **dynamically every time** `cost()` is called.
* `toString()` returns: `Rental[<name>, <days> days, $<cost formatted to 2 decimals>]`. Use `days` even if days is 1.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Single Day Rental)
tests.description: days = 1 must still output 1 days.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Zero Daily Rate)
tests.description: dailyRate = 0.0 uninsured for 3 days returns $45.00.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Decimal Cent Precision)
tests.description: Rates with fractional cents (e.g., $49.99) format cleanly to 2 decimals.

questions.title: Robust Item Count
questions.prompt:
Write a program in `Main.java`:

Ask `Enter items: ` until the user enters a whole number from `1` to `500` inclusive.
* For any input that cannot be parsed as an integer, print `Not an integer.`.
* For any integer outside `1` to `500`, print `Invalid count.`.
* When accepted, print `Accepted: ` followed by the number, then on the next line print `Total attempts: ` followed by the attempt count.
* Every prompt counts as one attempt. Never crash.

*Enter one input per line in the stdin box (the bracketed values in the sample).*
questions.sampleRun:
Enter items: dozen
Not an integer.
Enter items: 0
Invalid count.
Enter items: 45
Accepted: 45
Total attempts: 3
questions.expectedOutput:
Enter items: Not an integer.
Enter items: Invalid count.
Enter items: Accepted: 45
Total attempts: 3

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Huge Number Overflow)

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Zero and Negative Numbers)
tests.description: 0 and -5 print Invalid count..

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Exact Bounds)
tests.description: 1 and 500 accepted on attempt 1.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Decimal Input)
tests.description: 10.5 prints Not an integer..

questions.title: Rain Gauge Summary
questions.prompt:
`rainfall.txt` holds daily rainfall in millimeters per line: an integer `>= 0`. Read the file and write `rain_report.txt` with these four lines:

```
Days: <total lines>
Average: <average with exactly 2 decimal places>
Max rainfall: <largest value>
Dry days: <number of days with exactly 0 rainfall>
```

If `rainfall.txt` cannot be opened or does not exist, print `Cannot open rainfall.txt.` to the screen, write no report file, and terminate cleanly. `Main.java` holds an empty `main`; write your solution there.

*The grader creates `rainfall.txt` before running your code.*

questions.title: Executive Account
questions.prompt:
`BankAccount.java` is given and complete: `BankAccount(String owner, double balance)` with `getOwner()`, `getBalance()`, `double deposit(double amount)` (balance + amount), and `toString()` returning `Account[<owner>: $<balance formatted to 2 decimals>]`. It is provided as an extra tab — do not edit it.

Write `ExecutiveAccount.java`: an executive account **is a** `BankAccount` with an investment match.
* `ExecutiveAccount(String owner, double balance, double matchPercentage)`.
* `getMatchPercentage()` returns the match percentage (e.g. `5.0` for 5%).
* `deposit(double amount)`: calls `super.deposit(amount)` and additionally adds `amount * (matchPercentage / 100.0)` to the balance.
* `toString()` returns the parent's `toString()` followed by ` (Executive)`.
* Overrides **must** call `super.deposit(...)` and `super.toString()`. All new fields must be private.

tests.description: Super constructor, deposit with match bonus, toString() appending (Executive), polymorphic call.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Parent Recompilation Verification)
tests.description: If parent deposit changes, bypassing super.deposit(...) fails.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Zero Match)
tests.description: Match percentage 0.0 behaves identically to standard deposit.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Field Encapsulation)
tests.description: All new fields private.

Match percentage getter

Fields private

questions.title: Media Library Classifier
questions.prompt:
`Media.java`, `Movie.java`, and `Podcast.java` are given and read-only (provided as extra tabs):
* `Media(String title)` with `getTitle()`.
* `Movie extends Media`: has method `int getDurationMinutes()`.
* `Podcast extends Media`: has method `String getHost()`.

Write `MediaClassifier.java` containing two static methods:
* `static String describe(Media m)`:
  * For a `Movie`, returns `Movie: ` followed by title and duration in brackets (e.g. `Movie: Inception [148 mins]`).
  * For a `Podcast`, returns `Podcast: ` followed by title and host in parentheses (e.g. `Podcast: Daily (Host: Michael)`).
  * For any other `Media`, returns `Media: ` followed by title.
  * If `m` is `null`, return `"None"`.
* `static int countMovies(Media[] items)`: returns how many elements are instances of `Movie`. Safely ignores `null` elements.

Podcast: Daily (Host: Michael)
Media: Audiobook
1
